claims.text: Tungsten-containing refractory high-entropy alloys can retain high strength and hardness at elevated temperatures.
The conventional tungsten-based RHEA matrix lacks effective high-temperature self-lubrication.
The proposed intervention is to add small concentrations of Ti, Al, or other oxide-forming elements to a tungsten-based RHEA.
Ti or Al additions will react during high-temperature exposure in an oxidizing atmosphere to form stable oxide phases in situ.
The in situ oxides will be lubricious at high temperature.
The generated oxide precipitates or doped oxides will be coherent or semi-coherent with the alloy.
The generated oxides will form at the alloy surface or at grain boundaries during service.
Formation of the proposed lubricious oxide phases will reduce friction and wear.
The doped RHEA matrix will retain high mechanical strength while its oxide phases provide lubrication.
Relative to an undoped tungsten-based RHEA, the doped alloy will have a lower friction coefficient at high temperature.
Relative to an undoped tungsten-based RHEA, the doped alloy will have improved high-temperature wear resistance.
The doped alloy will maintain yield strength and hardness comparable to those of the undoped baseline.
The material will provide stable tribological performance from ambient temperature to above 1000 °C in oxidizing atmospheres.
RHEAs are vulnerable to oxidation, and their oxidation behavior depends strongly on alloy composition and testing conditions.
Excessive dopant concentrations or inappropriate dopant selection can produce excessive oxide formation and compromise mechanical strength.
The lubrication effectiveness will depend on the service conditions and oxidizing environment.
